findings.claim: A working directory that cannot be determined (for example a deleted cwd, where getcwd fails) now makes `roles append` refuse with "the binding of this checkout could not be read (getcwd: ...)". Before this commit that case returned the zero value and the append went through. T56 does not list this case. Its refusal rule names only a binding store that cannot be read, and says a cwd outside any repository goes as today. The new behavior is pinned by TestRolesAppendRefusesWhenTheWorkingDirectoryCannotBeDetermined, so it is deliberate, but it is a contract change beyond the task text. An agent that runs from a removed worktree directory gets a binding-read error although no binding was consulted. The task text should name this case, or the case should keep going as today.
proof_refs: engine/cmd/roles_bound.go:26-29 (new `return roles.BoundWorkflow{}, err` branch, previously `return roles.BoundWorkflow{}, nil`)

findings.claim: The `unreadable` helper calls t.Skip when the file is still readable at mode 000, as happens when the tests run as root. In that environment the two new unavailable-binding and unavailable-workflow-log tests skip silently. The new refusal branches at roles_bound.go:41-43 and 47-49 then have no coverage, and a green run is indistinguishable from a covered one. A fake or injected unavailable reader, or a non-permission way to make the file unavailable such as a symlinked file (which both stores classify as unavailable), would make the tests deterministic.
proof_refs: engine/projection/fsstore/store.go:187-189 and engine/workflow/filelog/store.go:179-181 (a symlinked file is classified unavailable without needing chmod)
